newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 31.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Governor Chris Patten criticised local tycoons for buckling under pressure from China and backing off their earlier statements of support for his political reforms, damaging Hong Kong's hopes for post-handover autonony.
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Hong Kong's domestic exports last year recorded their sharpest fall since 1960, with overall import and export growth hitting the lowest point in 14 years.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- The Preparatory Committee has decided to scrap parts of Hong Kong's Societies Ordinance and Public Order Ordinance, and leave it to the post-handover government to decide how to fill in the void.
-- "Internet bars" have become popular in Beijing, where young people could surf on the net, send messages and play games while enjoying a nice cup of coffee.

-- MING PAO -- Guangdong province was considering a further losening controls over foreign-invested enterprises selling their products on the domestic market. A plan would be announced in three months' time.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- China's National Electric Power Corp was to provide funds and guarantees to facilitate the financing of mainland power projects.

-- A leading property company said Hong Kong's luxury residential property market was expected to cool down this year compared with 1996 with transaction volumes falling and property prices increasing by 15 to 20 per cent.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD --China's five special economic zones averaged 14.3 percent growth last year, a cooling off from the explosive expansion in the last decade.
-- East and Southeast Asian economies would outperform the rest of the world this year on the back of robust investments and exports, but a report said their days of "super-normal" growth were over.
